title: 2024 AMC 10A Problem 20
statement:
Let \(S\) be a subset of \(\{1, 2, 3, \ldots, 2024\}\) such that the following two conditions hold:

• If \(x\) and \(y\) are distinct elements of \(S,\) then \(|x - y| \gt 2.\)

• If \(x\) and \(y\) are distinct odd elements of \(S,\) then \(|x - y| \gt 6.\)

What is the maximum possible number of elements in \(S?\)

solutions.text: The two conditions say chosen numbers are at least \(3\) apart, and chosen odd numbers at least \(7\) apart. Any four numbers in a block of \(10\) would need three gaps of at least \(3,\) so they would have to occupy positions \(r,r+3,r+6,r+9.\) Two of the odd entries would then differ by \(6,\) which is forbidden. Thus each full block of \(10\) contains at most \(3\) choices, and the last four positions contain at most \(2.\) This gives the upper bound \(202\cdot3+2=608.\) It is attained by the pattern \(1,4,8,11,14,18,\ldots\) (residues \(1,4,8\pmod{10}\)), together with \(2021,2024.\) Adjacent selected values differ by at least \(3,\) and the selected odd values are \(10\) apart. Therefore, the answer is C.
hints: Any two chosen numbers differ by at least \(3,\) and any two chosen odd numbers differ by at least \(7\)
A repeating block of \(10\) can hold at most \(3\) chosen numbers with only one odd; try residues \(1, 4, 8\)
